newsitem.title: UK: NatWest suspends 18 staff in flotation probe.
newsitem.headline: NatWest suspends 18 staff in flotation probe.

text.p: National Westminster Bank Plc said on Monday it had suspended 18 staff after an internal investigation unearthed suspected irregularities related to the flotation of insurance group Norwich Union.

"We carried out routine investigations and found one or two irregularities which made us suspicious and we thought there were grounds for further inquiries," Ivor Godfrey-Davies, head of external affairs at NatWest UK, said.

Norwich Union, an insurance and investment group, is planning to go public next year. It announced its flotation plans on October 2 and said people holding insurance policies sold before midnight on October 1 would be eligible for bonuses which analysts estimate at possibly 500 stg per policy.
It said policies in the pipeline -- signed before October 1 but not yet delivered to the company -- would also be eligible.

The NatWest staff, 10 financial advisers and eight administrators employed nationwide by Bristol-based NatWest Insurance Services, are thought to have backdated policies to qualify for bonuses, sources close to the investigation said.
Hayley Stimpson, press relations manager at Norwich Union, said Norwich had vetted applications in the pipeline and some had been rejected for not meeting the criteria.
She said the bulk of business came from independent financial advisers and declined to comment on reports of an upsurge in business in the week before October 1.
Godfrey-Davies said NatWest was keeping the Personal Investment Authority, the British personal investment industry watchdog, informed of the internal inquiry.
He said the probe was continuing and noted that no findings of guilt had yet been established.
Will Hastings, press officer at the PIA, confirmed the PIA was involved in an inquiry related to the flotation.
"PIA is in close liaison with Norwich Union and is looking at a number of cases to establish whether any misconduct has occurred," Hastings said.
He declined to give further details or comment on the possible scale of the suspected irregularities.
